title: Host-staged KV prefetch allocator and blocked-page eviction strategy
creator: Sasha Rivera
description:
Problem statement:

We need a robust, low-latency approach to operate oversized KV caches for long-context workloads without OOMing GPUs. Current continuous-batching experiments show good throughput but high tail latency and frequent OOMs under skewed token-length distributions. This ticket proposes a host-staged blocked-page allocator with coalesced prefetching and an "evict-on-read" soft-eviction policy to reduce peak GPU-resident working set while keeping generation latency within SLOs.

Goals:
- Avoid hard OOMs by providing a deterministic fallback path that moves cold KV blocks to pinned host staging buffers.
- Keep common hot prefixes resident on GPU via a small LRU-friendly hot slab and use coalesced async DMA for prefetching predicted contiguous blocks before decode.
- Make eviction behavior observable and tunable: watermarking, per-model budgets, and per-request backpressure when prefetch cannot keep up.
- Support graceful degradation: fallback model variant or lower-precision quantized variant when host-staging saturates.

Design summary:
1) Blocked-page layout: KV entries are written into fixed-size blocks (e.g., 128KB) mapped to contiguous GPU buffers where possible. Each block holds many small key-value slices for fast vectorized loads. Blocks are tagged with an epoch counter and residency flag.

2) Host-staging allocator: A pinned, page-locked host allocator holds evicted blocks. When a block is evicted, we issue an async cudaMemcpy (or equivalent DMA) from GPU->host pinned region and mark the block as "staged". Staged blocks are addressable by the runtime but incur a host access latency (microbenchmarked ~250-800us depending on PCIe/INF to GPU).

3) Coalesced prefetcher: The prefetcher operates on the continuous batch queue and heuristically coalesces predicted sequential block accesses from concurrent requests into single batched DMA transfers to GPU. Prefetch decisions use per-route hit-rate stats, recent KV offsets, and a simple RL-derived cost model that balances one-shot prefetch cost vs expected generation savings.

4) Evict-on-read soft eviction: Instead of immediate reclaim of all slices when memory pressure occurs, we perform prioritized eviction: cold blocks (low access frequency, old epochs) are moved first. If a request hits a staged block, we do one of: (a) synchronous pull to GPU with preemption costing latency; (b) serve from host with an annotation on response indicating degraded performance; or (c) fall back to alternate model variant when latency-critical.

5) Watermarks and backpressure: Two watermarks (soft/critical) per GPU. Soft triggers async prefetch throttling and increased staging, critical triggers backpressure on incoming batch acceptance or immediate fallback to cheaper model to prevent OOM.

6) NUMA and stream-aware allocators: For multi-GPU hosts, the allocator prefers local GPU staging buffers and uses per-stream pinned-page pools to maximize overlap between DMA and kernel execution.

7) Observability: Add residency histograms, eviction-rate metrics, per-block age distribution, and a new "KV staging latency" SLI. Integrate with console per-route breakdown to track customer impact.

Microbenchmarks (from local sim):
- Baseline (no staging) with 512-token median: throughput 12k tok/s, 99th-latency 420ms, OOM rate 0.9%.
- Host-staged prototype: throughput 10.8k tok/s, 99th-latency 610ms (when staging used), OOM rate 0.02%.
- Coalesced prefetch enabled: 11.6k tok/s, 99th-latency 480ms, host transfer bandwidth util improved 2.7x.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Host-staging increases tail latency on misses vs OOM avoidance. This is acceptable for many bursty services if we couple with graceful fallback.
- Pinned host memory consumption must be limited and accounted for in Dedicated capacity pricing.
- Prefetch heuristics risk wasted DMA for widely divergent batch accesses; RL model reduces wasted prefetch in simulations but needs live tuning.

Implementation plan (phases):
A. Prototype: implement pinned host allocator, async GPU->host evict path, and staged block metadata. Smoke tests for correctness and OOM avoidance. (2 weeks)
B. Prefetcher and coalescing: integrate with batching queue, implement cost model, metrics. (3 weeks)
C. Watermarks/backpressure and graceful fallback integration with routing layer. (2 weeks)
D. Load tests and canary rollout on dedicated capacity region, add Console dashboards + SLO alerts. (2 weeks)

Testing & validation:
- Synthetic replay with heavy long-context tails and Zipfian KV access patterns.
- A/B compare with real customer traces in staging (with opt-in) to measure perceived latency and correctness.
- Fault injection for DMA failures and simulating PCIe stalls.

Next steps / acceptance criteria:
- Prototype eliminates hard OOMs in nightly stress runs (>100k concurrent seqs) and reduces OOM rate by >95% vs baseline.
- Console shows per-route KV-stage hit/miss and staging-latency SLI instrumented.
- No memory leaks demonstrated after 24h continuous run.
